intro: Seven packs, pulled down and put through the game's own tracer at four angles: every model in every one of them is here, kept, grouped with the shapes it cannot be told apart from, or thrown out — with the number that decided it. The survey of where these packs came from is next door.

packs.title: Car Kit
packs.creator: Kenney
packs.alt: Low-poly vehicles laid out in rows: sedans, vans, trucks, a firetruck, tractors, karts and loose wheels.
packs.lede: The kit the game already draws from — traced whole, to see what was left behind.
packs.verdict: The kit is twice the fleet the game plays. Twenty-one vehicles survive and twelve are on the board, so nine are sitting in the zip: ambulance, garbage truck, luxury SUV, shovel and police tractors, the future racer, the flatbed truck, the flat delivery van and one kart. The five karts are one shape at 0.999 — oobi, oodi, ooli, oopi and oozi differ in paint alone, so four of them are dead weight. And the tightest four in the kit are not the four the game calls twins: ambulance, delivery, firetruck and van hold together at 0.85 where the sedan-taxi-police-sports set falls to 0.73 on its loosest pair.

packs.title: Cube Pets
packs.creator: Kenney
packs.alt: Twenty-four cube-bodied cartoon animals with big eyes, arranged in rows.
packs.lede: One cube, twenty-four animals. No props in the pack at all, so nothing is thrown out for not belonging.
packs.verdict: Twenty-one animals, and three that are already in the pack twice. Penguin is chick at 0.985, pig is dog at 0.964, polar bear is hog at 0.959 — one cube body, one recolour, and the tracer keeps neither. What is left is a fleet whose loosest pairing is still 0.58: even the crab and the elephant share the box. The names carry it — a player knows a penguin — and the ears do the telling apart.

packs.title: Watercraft Kit
packs.creator: Kenney
packs.alt: Low-poly boats: ocean liners, tall ships, a ghost galleon, tugs, house boats and rows of speedboats.
packs.lede: The harbour, and the question of which subset of it is a fleet.
packs.verdict: Thirty-two hulls, and the ghost ship is not one of them. ship-small-ghost is ship-small at 0.99: a green paint job on the same mesh. The ten speed boats do not collapse the way the preview suggests — they run 0.52 to 0.91 against each other, which is a twins tier with a whole difficulty path inside it. Take the subset the picker found and the fleet is four speed boats, four working boats, and the fan boat, the two sailing boats and the small ship to shout.

packs.title: Animated Cute Fish Pack
packs.creator: Quaternius
packs.alt: Rows of low-poly cartoon fish with oversized eyes, above wooden jetties and fishing rods.
packs.lede: Thirty-five species and seventeen pieces of fishing tackle, which the tracer has no trouble telling apart.
packs.verdict: Twenty-nine species, six of them thrown back. Goldfish and blue goldfish are one mesh at 1.00; royal gramma is the mandarin fish at 1.00; koi, turbot, butterfly fish and zebra clownfish all land above 0.95 on a fish already kept. What survives is the widest range of any pack here — 0.56 between swordfish and anglerfish, 0.89 between coral grouper and red snapper — and the tackle sorts itself out: seventeen rods, lures, docks and one worm, none of which is a fish.

packs.title: Food Kit
packs.creator: Kenney
packs.alt: A dense grid of low-poly food: fruit, vegetables, burgers, cakes, drinks, pots and kitchen tools.
packs.lede: Two hundred models and no single anatomy — a shelf of small ones instead.
packs.verdict: A hundred and forty-five survive, and most of them are spheres. The apple, the orange, the watermelon and the burger group at 0.87–0.91; the pot and the stew pot are 1.00; bowl and soup bowl are 1.00; cabbage and cauliflower are 0.995. The pack sells its variety in texture, and the tracer takes none of it. Thirty-four models are too thin to click — the cutlery, the chopsticks, the flat plates — and four lie too long on the board. There is a fleet in here, but it has to be picked against the silhouette rather than by reading the names: the round things are one shape wearing two hundred labels.

packs.title: Cars Pack
packs.creator: Quaternius
packs.alt: Eight low-poly cars in flat colours: sedans, a sports car, a police car, a taxi and an SUV.
packs.lede: A second artist's take on the same twelve the game already has.
packs.verdict: Seven cars, and no tier but twins. Every pair sits between 0.86 and 0.94; nothing in the pack shouts. They are also flatter than Kenney's — a median fill of 0.18 against 0.26 — so on the same board they take up less ink and bury more easily. As a set of extra twins they work; as a fleet they have no loud end, and mixing them into the Kenney yard would put two drawing styles on one board.

packs.title: Glasses Pack
packs.creator: iPoly3D
packs.alt: A set of low-poly spectacles and sunglasses in assorted frame shapes.
packs.lede: Twenty-eight pairs, twenty-six of them named nothing but "Glasses" — a pack where only the geometry can say what is what.
packs.verdict: The wrong shape class, and the number says so plainly. Twenty-eight pairs, and their silhouettes fill 5% to 15% of the frame — the ski goggles alone reach 27% — where the vehicles the game already draws fill 17% to 45%. Eighteen fall below the floor outright; the ten that pass only just, and the one model that is comfortably clickable is the ski goggles, which is a mask rather than a pair of spectacles. Two rims and a bridge is mostly air, and a click at small sizes would land between the lenses.
